description: Connecticut DL, structure taken from an issued credential. PII replaced.

provenance.source: PDF417 barcode decoded from an issued Connecticut driver's license (AAMVA v09, IIN 636006)
provenance.anonymization: Every identifying value was replaced with a placeholder of the same byte length and character class, so the encoded layout is byte-for-byte unchanged: DCS/DAC/DAD (names), DAQ (customer ID), DAG/DAI/DAK (address, CT ZIP prefix kept), DCF and DCK (which embed the issue date and the customer ID respectively), and DBB/DBD/DBA (dates, shifted). ZCB was replaced with zeros of the same length. DDB (card revision date) describes the card stock rather than the holder and is unchanged, as are DCA/DCB/DCD/DBC/DAU/DAY/DDA/DDE/DDF/DDG.
provenance.notes: Pins the part of the encoding that came from the card rather than from us: two directory entries instead of one, the element order (DAQ first, truncation flags interleaved with the names, DCK between DCG and DDA), DAK emitted as a bare 9-digit ZIP with no fixed-width space fill, DCK present at all, and a jurisdiction-defined ZC subfile following the DL subfile. Three deviations from the source card's raw bytes, all deliberate: (1) the card declares its DL subfile as 251 bytes where it holds 250, which also puts its declared ZC offset at 292 rather than 291 — the subfiles and the total length are right, only the boundary between them is off, and this vector carries our self-consistent arithmetic instead; (2) the card emits ZCA with an empty value, and this generator never writes an element it has no value for; (3) the source was a decoded field dump rather than the raw symbol, so trailing space padding inside an individual value could not be ruled out.
